NES Forge ${R.version} — ${R.name}

A standalone visual NES editor, assembler, ROM builder and experimental emulator. Alpha · Mobile Play candidate. Work through the existing tabs. Examples are ordinary editable project files included in the release package.

Start, open and recover

A fresh workspace starts with one blank scene. New Project creates a blank fixed room with the existing single-room build settings. Open Project loads a complete JSON or ZIP project. Browser recovery remains available through Restore / Dismiss; it is protected while being checked or awaiting your choice. New Project and Open Forge ROM have undoable replacement boundaries. A normal project open starts a new history.

Save your work

Save / Load use browser storage. Save Project As and Export create portable authoring backups, including worlds, tracker data, animations and the original imported ROM. Save As retains the existing location picker and download fallback. Cancel keeps the workspace. A save completing after you switch projects cannot rename or bind the newer workspace.

Project compatibility

Current projects use schema ${R.schema}. Supported older projects migrate with Gameplay Core disabled; their World and Audio Runtime settings are preserved when present. The frozen 1.8 editor rejects schema 12, protecting canonical actors, behaviors and scoped variables from silent loss. Unresolved behavior operations remain editable for repair and reject executable builds. Downgrade export is unsupported. Viewer/custom and single-room ROM formats remain layout 3, NFEX 1, MT16 1, WR16 3, MS16 2 and GP16 1. World ROMs retain layout 4 / WG17 version 1 and record their checked embedded source schema.

Project compatibility

replacements.before:
World builds use mapper 0, 32 KB PRG and 8 KB CHR. The profile allows at most 32 reachable worlds and 64 screens, subject to measured code, graphics, audio and compressed authoring capacity; many smaller projects can still exceed NROM. Canonical Gameplay Core actors in reachable destination Worlds/Rooms are linked and execute after transition; unreachable Actor Instances remain authoring data with an explicit diagnostic. Legacy scene actors outside the selected Player workflow, attack contacts and non-sound custom events remain authoring data. WG17 preserves the authoring snapshot except a previously imported ROM; keep JSON/ZIP backups for that original source.

Gameplay Core

GAMEPLAY CORE adds reusable Actor Definitions, authored Actor Instances and canonical structured state tables. Runtime Actors use transient generation-tagged slots; only explicitly declared Room or World variables persist across reconstruction. Definitions, placements, runtime memory and persistent records remain separate identities. Transition selection is deterministic by priority then authored order. Typed tables create, edit and remove every core record family without requiring project JSON edits.

Every condition/action and known component field has a canonical typed schema shared by the table UI and compiler. Executable validation rejects missing, malformed, out-of-range, invalid-reference or type-incompatible values before code generation; values are not silently clamped, masked or coerced into bytes. The selected generated profile rejects canonical operations it cannot execute rather than compiling silent no-ops. The mapper-0 profile permits 12 executable Actor Instances total, including the Sideview compatibility Player, and 64 one-byte persistent values. Overflow rejects; there is no actor streaming.

The five starter recipes are Sideview Player, Ground Patrol Enemy, Stationary Contact Hazard, Collectible Pickup and Switch + Door. Recipes create ordinary editable canonical records. Enable Gameplay Core explicitly to compile supported generic actor behavior into single-room or World generated runtimes. Only enabled components provide executable capabilities; disabling Behavior leaves placement/rendering intact but performs no entry/tick/exit actions, transitions, timer work, persistent writes or behavior damage. Behavior actions own ContactDamage operands, and Actor Instance bindings own persistence routing; any component mirrors must agree. The Sideview Player compatibility binding keeps existing Player/Target settings and selects the retained Player executor for movement, collision and animation; this is not full generic-runtime Player unification. Projectiles, moving platforms, checkpoints, dialogue, ladders, one-way platforms, richer combat and the visual behavior graph are not part of 1.9.0.

Switch + Door remains an alpha persistence/identity proof. syncActiveFromPersistent may deactivate an active actor, but reversal takes effect only after reconstruction because inactive actors do not evaluate. This is not physical Door blocking or a reversible gate system.

ROM opening, playback and capture

Open Forge ROM retains generated bytes for Run Original, but recovery depends on the backend. A World layout-4/WG17 ROM restores its checked embedded project source losslessly. A single-room layout-3/GP16 ROM opens with explicit partial recovery: scenes, art, retained bindings and legacy gameplay settings are reconstructed, but Gameplay Core source is not embedded and therefore reopens disabled/empty. Use native JSON/ZIP backups for complete schema-12 authoring recovery. Import ROM keeps its existing append/capture behavior for older and other ROMs; a World ROM instead requires Open Forge ROM. Other ROMs can be inspected through supported emulator/capture/disassembly paths; their original maps and logic are not automatically reconstructed. Runtime / Hybrid capture retain provenance-based background and sprite data. Bake Visible Frame is the existing visible-image conversion; exact raster captures may require validated static conversion for building.

Audio Runtime and Studio

AUDIO edits the existing tracker and instrument envelopes and previews them in the browser. Enable Audio Runtime to compile pulse 1, pulse 2, triangle and noise music into generated viewer, single-room or World ROMs. Named SFX reuse one pattern channel and row range; an animation frame's sound event references its stable SFX ID or unique name and starts once on frame entry. One SFX plays at a time and temporarily owns its selected channel before music resumes. DPCM samples and tracker effect commands are not implemented and fail when executable rather than disappearing.

MIDI and uncompressed score-partwise MusicXML import append ordinary tracker patterns and instruments, then select the imported song order. Existing SFX patterns remain in place. Notes are quantized to sixteenth-note rows; one song tempo is retained; excess polyphony beyond three tonal voices plus one noise voice is rejected. Compressed MXL, score transcription, tablature, alternate audio models and automatic Audio Runtime enablement are not included.

Assembly

CODE retains official 6502 assembly, labels, macros and segmented .org output. Audio Runtime is available only in generated code paths; enable authored custom assembly or Audio Runtime, not both. Disassembly inspects the mapped CPU window; it is not a recovered source project.

Mobile play and controllers

In EMULATOR, open Play view to expand the loaded ROM and controls together. Run/Pause controls emulation; NES Start and Select are separate game buttons. Touch controls support a direction with A/B and simultaneous A+B. Show or hide touch controls as needed. Fullscreen is requested by a button; where the browser declines or lacks support, the expanded player stays usable inside the browser. Exit returns to the editor without rebuilding or resetting the ROM.

Connect a compatible wired/USB-C controller or pair Bluetooth in the device's settings, then press a controller button while this page is focused. Controller settings select one gamepad and map its buttons/axes to the eight NES controls. Availability depends on the device, browser and controller. After interruptions, release the controller to neutral before pressing again. Physical-device acceptance remains documented separately in the package; no universal compatibility claim is made.

Audio interchange and workshop

Listening and external-software acceptance remain separate.

Native graphics recovery

General ROM Analysis inspects unknown engines independently of the emulator. In Raw CHR patterns, Preview native tile import then Import as new tile sheet adds editable physical CHR-ROM tiles with saved source SHA-256/range evidence. The generated grayscale sheet is excluded from builds by default; its palette/layout do not recover original maps. Download active sheet CHR exports edited bitplanes. CHR RAM, compressed graphics, native maps, collision and Audio need other supported methods; generic inspection is not universal recovery.

Checkpoints and reversible experiments

For a ROM loaded in EMULATOR, RE runtime tools can save bounded full-machine Checkpoints, run explicit controller-input scripts and apply reversible RAM byte edits. Restoring rewinds CPU/PPU/APU/video state and clears stale observations. Reset or ROM replacement clears session checkpoints. Active experiment rollback checkpoints cannot be deleted. Scripts replay inputs; they do not discover stages, health or enemy semantics. I/O and ROM/mapper register patches are rejected.
